title: TaskClass
description: REVIEW REQUIRED — encodes the research decision of what a task class is. One classification of one UNIT of agent work, where the unit itself is an unsettled research question with three candidates: prompt, segment, session. The unit is therefore explicit and required on every record, and classifications at multiple granularities over the same underlying data are expected to coexist — that coexistence is what lets unit choices be compared empirically. Record identity is (unit, unit_ref, classifier_version, taxonomy_version); records differing in any of those are distinct observations, not duplicates. The three axes (task_type, context_breadth, risk) are a DRAFT taxonomy to pressure-test in interviews, not settled fact; values marked PROVISIONAL below were added because real local sessions did not fit the original eight types, and can be deleted at review. Uncertainty is first-class: confidence is required, 'unclassified' is a legal outcome, every axis has 'unknown'.

taxonomy_version.description: Version of the taxonomy itself, independent of schema and classifier versions — the taxonomy WILL change after engineer interviews, and old labels must remain interpretable.

classifier_version.description: Version of the classifier (ruleset or model) that produced this label.

unit.description: The granularity of what was classified. Deliberately unsettled at v0: per-prompt (one user prompt and the agent's response window), per-segment (a run of turns split by observable boundaries — see session.schema segments and conventions.md), per-session (the whole log). Distributions computed at different units are compared, not assumed equal.

unit_ref.description: Exactly what was classified. Turn indices are 0-based ordinals over USER PROMPT turns as defined in conventions.md (tool results, meta records, and command output are not turns).

turn_range.description: Inclusive. Required for unit=prompt (start_turn == end_turn) and unit=segment; null for unit=session.

segment_id.description: Required when unit=segment; must match a segment in the session record produced by the same segmenter_version.

segmenter_version.description: Required when unit=segment: version of the observable boundary rules (conventions.md) that produced the segment. Segment classifications are only comparable within a segmenter_version.

status.description: 'unclassified' is a legal, reportable outcome — the classifier declining to guess. 'ambiguous' means a label was assigned but alternatives were close; alternatives[] must be populated.

task_type.description: Null iff status=unclassified. PROVISIONAL values from real-data pressure-testing: 'ui_verification_loop' (observed: a 12MB session dominated by browser-automation tool calls iterating on visual behavior — huge session, modest diff; none of the original eight fit) and 'agent_meta_work' (observed: sessions configuring/orchestrating the agent tooling itself). 'other' requires other_note.

other_note.description: Required free text when task_type='other'. These notes are interview material — a recurring other_note is a missing taxonomy value.

context_breadth.description: CAVEAT from real data: cross_repo is nearly invisible in local logs (one session = one cwd); it will be under-detected until multi-repo enterprise telemetry exists. 'unknown' is expected to be common at v0.

risk.description: Risk kept as two independent axes, never combined into one tier score.

test_coverage.description: CAVEAT: unvalidatable against local data — zero of the observed local projects had test suites, so this axis collapses to one value outside enterprise repos.

criticality.description: Requires org context (deploy targets, service tiers) no local log contains; 'unknown' until trace/enterprise data supplies it.

confidence.description: Required even when unclassified (confidence that no label applies).

alternatives.description: Runner-up labels with their confidences. Mandatory when status='ambiguous'. Preserves disagreement instead of erasing it.

method.description: Glass box: how the label was produced.

rationale.description: Human-readable why, referencing only content-free features.

features_used.description: Names of the content-free session features the decision consumed (e.g. 'diff_stats.files_touched', 'tool_call_pattern'). Enforces and documents the no-content rule per record.
